headache = a pain in your head
toothache = a pain in a tooth
stomachache = a pain in your stomach
sore throat = pain in the throat, often with a cold
runny nose = when liquid comes from your nose because of a cold
cough = forcing air from your throat, often when you have a cold
temperature = how hot your body is; a high one means you are ill
flu = a serious illness with fever, aches and tiredness
catch a cold = to become ill with a common cold
feel sick = to feel as if you might vomit
dizzy = feeling that you might fall, as if the room is spinning
bruise = a dark mark on the skin after a hit
cut = an injury where the skin is broken by something sharp
plaster = a small sticky covering for a cut
bandage = a strip of cloth used to cover an injury
prescription = a written order from a doctor for medicine
chemist = a shop that sells medicine
GP = a general doctor you visit first
appointment = an arranged time to see a doctor or dentist
dentist = a person who looks after your teeth
healthy lifestyle = habits that keep your body well, such as exercise and good food
put on weight = to become heavier
lose weight = to become lighter
allergic to = becoming ill when you eat or touch something
vaccination = an injection that protects you from a disease
first aid = simple medical help given before a doctor arrives
ambulance = a vehicle that takes sick or injured people to hospital
emergency = a serious situation that needs help immediately
painkiller = medicine that reduces pain
recover = to get better after an illness
get over = to become well again after an illness
check-up = a regular visit to a doctor when you are not ill
hurt = to feel pain; to cause pain
broken bone = a bone that has cracked or snapped
feel better = to start recovering after being ill
see a doctor = to visit a doctor because you are ill
hospital = a place where doctors treat people who are very ill or injured
ward = a large room in a hospital with several beds
surgery = a doctor's office; also an operation
A&E = the hospital department for sudden serious problems
operation = when a surgeon cuts the body to repair something
surgeon = a doctor who does operations
injection = medicine put into the body with a needle
tablet = a small solid piece of medicine you swallow
medicine = a substance you take to get better
drops = liquid medicine you put in your eyes or nose
ointment = a thick cream you put on the skin
ill = not healthy; feeling unwell
sick = ill; also feeling as if you might vomit
disease = a serious illness, often with a name
infection = an illness caused by bacteria or a virus
virus = a tiny thing that can make you ill
bacteria = tiny living things; some cause infection
symptom = a change in the body that shows you are ill
fever = a body temperature that is too high because you are ill
sneeze = to suddenly blow air from your nose
ache = a continuous pain that is not sharp
pain = an unpleasant feeling when something is wrong in the body
bleed = to lose blood from a cut
wound = an injury where the skin is broken
sprain = an injury when you twist a joint too far
swell = to become larger because of injury or illness
itch = an uncomfortable feeling that makes you want to scratch
rash = red spots or patches on the skin
asthma = an illness that makes it hard to breathe
inhaler = a small device that sends medicine into the lungs
diabetes = an illness where the body cannot control sugar in the blood
hay fever = sneezing and itchy eyes caused by pollen
food poisoning = illness from eating bad or dirty food
sunburn = red, painful skin after too much sun
burn = an injury from heat or fire
faint = to become unconscious for a short time
unconscious = not awake and not able to respond
conscious = awake and able to understand what is happening
breathe = to take air in and out of your lungs
pulse = the beat of blood that you can feel in your wrist or neck
blood pressure = the force of blood as it moves through the body
X-ray = a picture of bones inside the body
crutches = sticks you put under your arms to help you walk
wheelchair = a chair with wheels for people who cannot walk
sling = a cloth that holds an injured arm against the body
stitches = thread used to close a deep cut
plaster cast = a hard covering that keeps a broken bone still
ice pack = a cold bag you put on a swelling
thermometer = an instrument that measures body temperature
stethoscope = the instrument a doctor uses to listen to your heart and lungs
waiting list = a list of people who must wait for treatment
specialist = a doctor who knows a lot about one part of the body
optometrist = a person who tests your eyesight
glasses = lenses in a frame that help you see better
contact lenses = small lenses you put on your eyes instead of glasses
hearing aid = a small device that helps you hear
disabled = having a condition that makes some activities harder
disabled toilet = a larger toilet with extra space and support
mental health = how well your mind and feelings are
stress = worry and pressure that can make you feel ill
anxious = worried and nervous, often for a long time
depressed = very sad for a long time and unable to enjoy things
insomnia = when you cannot sleep well for many nights
exhausted = extremely tired
rest = time when you are not active so the body can recover
diet = the food you usually eat; also eating less to lose weight
obese = very overweight in a way that is bad for health
underweight = weighing less than is healthy
get fit = to become healthier and stronger through exercise
addiction = when you cannot stop a harmful habit
smoking = breathing in smoke from cigarettes
give up smoking = to stop using cigarettes
alcohol = drinks such as beer or wine that can make you drunk
drunk = having had too much alcohol
drugs = illegal substances, or medicine in some contexts
hygiene = keeping yourself and things clean to stay healthy
wash your hands = to clean your hands with soap and water
brush your hair = to pull a brush through your hair
fill a tooth = when a dentist repairs a hole in a tooth
braces = wires that a dentist uses to straighten teeth
dentist chair = the special chair you sit in at the dentist
blood test = when a nurse takes blood to check your health
sick note = a paper from a parent or doctor that explains an absence
stay in bed = to rest in bed because you are ill
take your temperature = to use a thermometer to see if you have a fever
call an ambulance = to phone emergency services for a vehicle to hospital
emergency number = the phone number you call for police, fire or ambulance
first-aid kit = a box of plasters, bandages and basic medical things
side effect = an unwanted result of taking medicine
dose = the amount of medicine you should take at one time
get well soon = something you say or write to a person who is ill
